title: Catalog priority lanes and enterprise adapter triage for customer model requests
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Problem: Enterprise customers are submitting heterogeneous model requests (new model adds, urgent version pin requests, depreciation asks) via multiple channels (support, CSM, GitHub). Current intake funnels lack clear SLA lanes and tailored eval requirements for regulated customers, causing ad-hoc engineering work and late-stage rollbacks. Goal: Define explicit priority lanes and an 'enterprise adapter' triage flow inside the model catalog intake that maps customer signals to prescriptive onboarding steps, eval gates, and release/deprecation policies. Deliverables: 1) Priority lane definitions (Fastpass, Standard, Regulated) with SLA and acceptance criteria. 2) A decision table to map customer signals (SLA, PHI/PCI risk, model changes magnitude, rollback difficulty) to lane and to required eval suite. 3) A version-pinning policy and temporary pin workflow for enterprise customers that minimizes engineering overhead. 4) An automated checklist that surfaces required artifacts (security review, eval report, audit logs) in intake tickets. 5) Playbook and template responses for CSMs/support to set expectations.
comments: 2026-02-20 Sofia Nguyen: Created ticket after weekly GTM sync. Noted repeated ask from 3 enterprise CSMs for predictable pinning timeframe and clearer deprecation notices. Linked customer cases in Confluence.

2026-02-24 Liam Patel: Ran quick audit of the last 30 catalog requests. Preliminary findings: ~40% of enterprise requests include a requested pin; 25% require security review; average time-to-onboard for enterprise is 21 days vs 7 for public catalog. Updated spreadsheet in attachments.

2026-03-01 Product review: Decided to introduce three lanes: Fastpass (one-week SLA for critical business continuity pins), Standard (2–3 week onboarding), Regulated (4–8 week with mandatory compliance & audit). Trade-offs discussed: Fastpass reduces safety margin; require auto-rollback windows and postmortem commitments.

2026-03-04 Design feedback (Ava Martinez): Suggested intake UI changes: explicit radio buttons for 'Regulated workload', 'Requires pin', and auto-checklist expansion. Mockups in design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design/pull/402

2026-03-07 Eng feedback (Priya Rao): Engine constraints noted for temporary pin mechanism — needs allocation token to prevent eviction by autoscaler. Proposed scoped infra task ENG-19876. Recommended adding a 'pin expiry' metadata field.
2026-03-10 Legal review request submitted: security_review_required flagged for Regulated lane. Expect 5 business day review. Added templated legal checklist to Confluence.
2026-03-12 Liam Patel: Draft playbook posted. Next: validate decision table against 5 historical customer cases and run tabletop with Solutions Engineers on 2026-03-17.

Open questions: What telemetry do we need to detect pin-related regressions? Can we automate 'pin expiry' enforcement into Dedicated capacity leases? How do we price Fastpass pins for fairness and cost recovery?
acceptance_criteria: Priority lanes documented with explicit SLA and required artifacts for each lane
Decision table mapping customer signals to lane, eval gates, and release steps published
Temporary pin workflow defined (including pin metadata, expiry enforcement, and rollback steps)
Intake form mockups and templates merged into Catalog UI repo
Pilot: validate flow with 3 enterprise customers and measure time-to-acknowledge and time-to-onboard
